events.did: sent Victor her location pin while steadying Sydney and tugging the blindfold off
events.quote_anchor: “I’m doing it,” she said, sending him a pin as the girl on the bench began to stir, rolling over in her sleep.

events.did: looked down at the girl on the bench and saw that the blond, heart-shaped girl was not Sydney
events.quote_anchor: She had Sydney’s blond hair. Her heart-shaped face. But it wasn’t her.

events.did: ended up in her favorite diner booth at home, emptying sachets into her coffee until the spoon stood up straight
events.quote_anchor: she was sitting in her favorite booth, emptying sachet after sachet into her coffee, waiting to see how many it would take for the spoon to stand up straight.

relations.quote_anchor: She was strapped to the bench, blindfolded and hands bound, an IV running into her wrist.

relations.did: traded the soldier’s body for one of her own default bodies that Sydney had seen before and would trust
relations.quote_anchor: Auburn hair in dark-wash jeans. A body Sydney had seen before. One she’d recognize, and trust.

relations.did: refused to force Sydney to come with her, unlike before
relations.quote_anchor: But Syd wasn’t a flag in a game, something to be stolen. If she wanted to come with June, that was one thing, but she wouldn’t force her.

relations.did: is Sydney’s older sister, the role June had stepped into because the original was dead
relations.quote_anchor: The one she worshipped, idolized. The one June, in some ways, had replaced, stepping into the vacant role because the original was dead.
